title: bn254-pairing-inversion: measured GT rho plus G1 scalar multiplication, 2^130.799212

claims.statement: For the full-production bn254-pairing-inversion challenge, the single-trial algorithm of proof.md returns a G1 point P and the fixed profile generator Q0 with e(P,Q0)=z, with success probability at least 0.85 over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins, and every run performs at most W < 2^130.799212 units, where one unit is C=20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents. The algorithm recovers x = dlog_g(z) with the 32-adding Pollard-rho walk of the shipped tower implementation, computes P=[x]P0 on the profile curve y^2=x^3+3 with Jacobian double-and-add, sets Q=Q0, and verifies g^x=z, P on-curve and [r]P=O; the pair is valid by bilinearity e(P,Q0)=e(P0,Q0)^x=g^x=z. The per-step price 52,000 instructions is a 1.1007x charge over the Valgrind Callgrind measurement (47,238.44 Ir) of the shipped scalar C tower walk. The capped work counts the 3N walk steps (N=2*ceil(sqrt(r))), N Floyd comparisons, all setup and table construction, the measured G1 scalar multiplication (Callgrind 1,062,076 Ir for the whole point process, charged at 2^24), verification, output and recovery; no work is amortised and no preprocessing is free. Success relies on the disclosed standard r-adding random-map heuristic with the 31/32 correction and is bounded below by 0.85; the protected minimum 0.39 is met. Memory is below 2^20 bytes and no non-uniform advice is used.

experiments.purpose: Recompute every ledger row from the profile order, check the declared rational is the rounded-up log2(W) and that the 0.85 success bound holds, recompute the shipped G1 vectors with an independent affine implementation on the real BN254 curve (on-curve, order r, exact match), and run the same 32-adding walk on small prime additive groups as scope-limited correctness and statistics evidence.
